content.title: About
content.content: Ground beef is finely chopped meat obtained from various cuts of a cow. A patty made from this ground beef is a shaped portion, usually pan‑fried or baked. The product has a rich meaty flavor, firm texture, and high protein content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ground beef is a staple in many national dishes, from American burgers to Italian Bolognese sauce.
Beef patties can be seasoned with herbs, spices, and vegetables for varied taste profiles.
Traditionally the grind comes from shoulder, neck, or round cuts, which provide a balance of lean meat and fat for juiciness.
In some cultures beef is considered a “leaner” option compared with pork because of its lower saturated‑fat content.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Beef provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef contains heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Ground beef supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Zinc and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals aid immune function and antioxidant defenses.

items.title: Creatine
items.content: Beef naturally contains creatine, beneficial for muscle strength and endurance.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Ground beef can be high in saturated fat; choosing lean varieties helps limit intake.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Raw meat may harbor pathogens such as Salmonella or E. coli; cook to an internal temperature of at least 71 °C.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to beef.

items.title: Additives
items.content: Pre‑packaged ground beef may contain preservatives, flavor enhancers, or fillers that not everyone tolerates.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Beef patties can be pan‑fried over medium heat until a golden crust forms, baked in the oven, or grilled. Serve with vegetables, sauces, in burgers, or use in stews and soups.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep ground beef refrigerated at 0‑4 °C for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight container at ‑18 °C, where it remains good for 3‑4 months. Thaw frozen meat in the refrigerator before cooking.
